definitions: as found in nature and not involving anything made or done by people :
A natural ability or characteristic is one that you were born with:
(of a person or their behaviour ) seeming normal and relaxed :
Natural food or drink is pure and has no chemical substances added to it and is therefore thought to be healthy :
a parent who caused someone to be born , although possibly not their legal parent or the parent who raised them:
examples: a natural substance
People say that breast-feeding is better than bottle-feeding because it's more natural.
He died from natural causes (= because he was old or ill )
Floods and earthquakes are natural disasters .
Most people go on safari to see wild animals in their natural habitat .
Choose a dress in a natural fibre such as silk , linen or cotton to keep you cool .

definitions: information or reports about recent events :
a television or radio programme consisting of reports about recent events :
to tell someone about something bad that has just happened and may have an effect on them:
to be someone or something that will affect a person or situation well/ badly :
to be reported about:
examples: That's the best piece of news I've heard for a long time !
We've had no news of them since they left for Australia .
Have you heard the news about Tina and Tom ? They're getting divorced .
I can't wait to hear all your news.
The news that
We've got some good news for you. We're getting married .

definitions: the things that a person must have in order to have a satisfactory life or accomplish something:
the things you must have for a satisfactory life :
examples: Housing and education are basic needs.
They don't have enough food to meet their needs.
He was struggling to meet the needs of his growing family .
The educational needs of children today aren't much different from the educational needs of children historically.
What sorts of training needs do our new employees have, and how can we meet them?
the special needs of the disabled

definitions: needed in order to achieve a particular result :
used in negatives and questions to show that you disapprove of something and do not think it should be used or done:
A necessary evil is something unpleasant that must be accepted in order to achieve a particular result :
Necessary can be used in negatives and questions to show that you disapprove of something and do not think it should be done:
examples: He lacks the necessary skills for the job .
I don't have much time so I won't be staying any longer than necessary.
Just do what's necessary and then leave .
We don't want to take any more luggage with us than is strictly
I don't think that kind of language is necessary in a show that kids could be watching .
Don’t take any more luggage than is strictly necessary.

definitions: relating to or typical of a whole country and its people , rather than to part of that country or to other countries :
someone who officially belongs to a particular country :
relating to all parts of a nation or to a nation as a whole rather than to any part of it:
a citizen of a particular country :
relating to countries or to one particular country :
examples: a national holiday
Britain has more than ten national newspapers .
The company's national headquarters is in Rome.
The children were wearing traditional national costume / dress
The government's view is that raising taxes now would not be in the national interest
30 people , including six Mexican nationals, were killed in yesterday's plane crash .

definitions: being the first one after the present one or after the one just mentioned :
immediately after:
The time when you next do something is the first time you do it again:
used when describing two people or things that are very close to each other with nothing between them:
used to mean `after' when making a choice or a comparison :
examples: Who works in the office next to yours?
Take the next street on the right .
Who do you think will be the next president ?
Nothing really changes around here. One day is pretty much like the next.
(The) next time you want to borrow something, please ask me first.
I'm so busy it's hard to remember what I'm supposed to be doing from one minute to the next.

definitions: all the animals , plants , rocks , etc. in the world and all the features , forces , and processes that happen or exist independently of people , such as the weather , the sea , mountains , the production of young animals or plants , and growth :
the force that is responsible for physical life and that is sometimes spoken of as a person :
the type or main characteristic of something:
to be usual and expected :
a person's character :
examples: her love of nature
This new technique of artificially growing cells copies what actually happens in nature.
a nature article / book / programme
Feeling tired-out is Nature's way of telling you to rest .
Nature gave these tiny creatures the ability to reproduce quickly when food is abundant .
What was the nature of his enquiry ?

definitions: necessary or wanted :
examples: After six hours work in the garden , we sat down for a much-needed rest .
Most people like to feel needed.
much-needed After six hours work in the garden , we sat down for a much-needed rest .

definitions: not anything:
to be a matter or subject that someone has no good reason to know about or be involved with:
to have or want no connection or influence with someone or something:
to have no importance or value :
free or without paying :
examples: There's nothing in the drawer - I took everything out.
Nothing I could say would cheer her up.
I have nothing new to tell you.
There's nothing else (= no other thing)
There's nothing much (= not very much)
The story was nothing but (= only)

definitions: the substances that you take into your body as food and the way that they influence your health :
the process of taking in and using food , or the scientific study of this:
the process by which the body takes in and uses food , esp . food that it needs to stay healthy , or the scientific study of this process
examples: Good nutrition is essential if patients are to make a quick recovery .
improvements in nutrition
She's a professor of nutrition at Columbia University.
good nutrition Good nutrition is essential if patients are to make a quick recovery .

definitions: a long printed story about imaginary characters and events :
new and original , not like anything seen before:
used to refer to a new strain (= type ) of a virus that has not been seen before:
a long , printed story about imaginary characters and events :
new and original ; not like anything seen before:
examples: Have you read any of Jane Austen's novels?
His latest novel is selling really well.
What needs do romantic novels fulfil , and why do they have such wide appeal ?
a novel idea / suggestion
Keeping a sheep in the garden is a novel way of keeping the grass short !
The COVID-19 pathogen is a novel coronavirus.
